newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast heavy crudes off on oversupply talk.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast heavy crudes off on oversupply talk.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes remained flat as refiners took in South American grades while heavy grades fell amid trader talk of increased supply.
Chevron and Texaco lowered their California posted prices for Point Arguello offshore crude by 50 cents a barrel late Wednesday.

One trader said the increasing supply of Outer Continetal Shelf crude, like Point Arguello, was swelling heavy crude supplies. He assessed markets between 10 to 20 cents below postings, 15 cents lower than recent deals.

In light crude, West Coast spot crude traders focused on Oriente, an Ecuadorian grade which Texaco offered for late April delivery at $1.35 to $1.40 a barrel under Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, traders said.
A trader familiar with Texaco's shipments said Glencore trading house offered at $1.50 under ANS.
Texaco's offer follows its purchase of a 400,000 barrel cargo of ANS on Friday. The price, $1.32 off May WTI, is 0.27-cent widening from the last deal.
Outright prices stood at $17.93/18.13 a barrel, 25 cents off Tuesday.
A leading seller of ANS priced shipments at $0.95 cents under WTI.
